name: Andrej Karpathy
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Industry accounts for over 90% of notable models, and academia can hardly get in; the bottleneck is data/algorithmic efficiency, not architecture, and the foundation is still important
D01.late_modes: Merely piling on compute to catch up with the leading models; concentration is still rising

D02.one_line: RLVR mainly resamples existing abilities and introduces no new reasoning patterns; I am bearish on RL itself and bullish on the environment layer of data
D02.late_modes: Generic RLVR tuning papers with no data or environment of their own

D03.one_line: Continual learning is the ability I named as missing in agents; measurements show that seventy to ninety percent of the cost of automated improvement is compute, not the method itself
D03.late_modes: Packaging an automated-improvement pipeline on a fixed small benchmark as a breakthrough
D03.conflict: Invests in the RL environment platform Prime Intellect

D04.one_line: On SWE-bench the gap between the full agent and the bare model is only 2.4 points, which shows that the general harness is being absorbed by the model itself
D04.late_modes: Building a general agent framework/scaffold will be absorbed by models and products
D04.conflict: His employer Anthropic makes Claude Code

D05.one_line: LMArena grew from a Berkeley student project to a $3.1B valuation, showing that evaluation by itself can be built into something big independently
D05.late_modes: Hand-running a one-off leaderboard to hold a spot, with no robustness check

D06.one_line: SO-101, hardware at roughly the $230 level, lets academia afford a real-robot closed loop for the first time, no longer limited to demonstrations
D06.late_modes: Only tuning on standard benchmarks, with no analysis of new failure modes

D07.one_line: OpenVLA-OFT is 15 points higher than the diffusion head on real robots; this line already has real-robot validation and is past the demo stage
D07.late_modes: Treating diffusion policy as the only orthodoxy and not comparing against simple baselines

D08.one_line: That a representation can be read out does not mean the policy actually uses it, and this is still unproven; the X3 table independently corroborates that AMI Labs/General Intuition valuations run ahead of this layer of evidence
D08.late_modes: Selling interactive video generation as a visual product, waiting to be absorbed by general models

D09.one_line: MimicGen-style amplification of real seeds has a low bar, but after the debate it is confirmed that the weakness is wider than contact/touch: any unmodeled fine-grained physics will be exposed
D09.late_modes: Claiming simulation data is 'unlimited' without giving verifiable metrics
D09.conflict: Invests in the RL environment platform Prime Intellect

D10.one_line: Tesla's first safety report has just self-reported zero casualties but has not been independently audited; fleet-type tracks are simply closed to academia
D10.late_modes: An individual or small team building an end-to-end demo, with no fleet and no long-tail data
D10.conflict: Former Tesla AI director; has publicly been bullish on Tesla

D11.one_line: BLINK/VSI-Bench show models are close to blind guessing on basic spatial tasks, a clean and verifiable gap
D11.late_modes: Only chasing existing VQA scores, with no error analysis

D12.one_line: Sora2 shut down its app/API within a year, confirming that thin-wrapper consumer apps get absorbed; the underlying technology itself is still advancing
D12.late_modes: Building thin-wrapper text-to-image/text-to-video consumer apps with no data loop

D13.one_line: SAEs do worse than linear probes out of distribution, and CoT monitoring is fragile; the verification problem is more fundamental than any method itself
D13.late_modes: Treating a popular interpretability method as the only orthodoxy and not comparing against simple baselines
D13.conflict: Current Anthropic employee; touches his employer's safety research

D14.one_line: FlashAttention shows a small academic team can produce a standard component, but most infra work needs an industrial feedback loop, so the window is narrow

D15.one_line: Subproblems that can be scored automatically (AlphaEvolve) will speed up first; in fields lacking a feedback loop, deep models still cannot beat simple baselines

D16.one_line: Industry has already put generative recommendation online (Tencent TGR), but its compute cost may be 10-100 times that of traditional models; it is an enterprise data-loop business

lever_reason: Verification and data engines (simulation + real data) decide whether capability can land in the physical world; RL and architecture themselves are not the bottleneck, and scaled pre-training is the foundation but not the only lever

Q2.condition: Narrow-domain model + a complementary team of 2-4 + GPUs sustained over months + open weights that outsiders can adopt; if no ready-made evaluation exists, build your own; the X2 debate confirmed this also counts as a contribution

cruxes.question: Is evaluation/verification a more upstream bottleneck than the scale of real data?
cruxes.my_position: It is the precondition; without credible verification, the gains from data, simulation and RL cannot each be confirmed
cruxes.would_change_if: A lab makes a big capability leap with its evaluation methods completely unchanged, and it is later agreed that evaluation really did not matter

cruxes.question: Can an academic lab training a narrow-domain foundation model get real outside adoption, or is it just amusing itself?
cruxes.my_position: Yes, but only for narrow domain + open weights + a small complementary team; the X2 table's debate confirmed that when no ready-made evaluation exists, building your own evaluation itself counts as a contribution; academia still cannot get into general pre-training
cruxes.would_change_if: An academic project at the scale of Stanford Marlowe (about 250 H100s) is widely adopted externally, or there is none for two consecutive years

cruxes.question: Are the representations learned by JEPA/world models actually used by policies to make decisions, or can they be read out but not used?
cruxes.my_position: Doubt by default, with a middling score based on inference; demo-level reconstruction quality is not evidence
cruxes.would_change_if: An ablation shows that removing or perturbing the representation significantly lowers closed-loop control success

taste_advice: First ask whether it can be gamed, then whether it looks good; what simulation taught me is how a simulator lies

pairwise.why: Verification is the precondition and the bar for academia is lower; after the debate D08 drops again to 5, so the gap is larger
Evaluation produces credible results faster than embodied work, and the bar for academia is lower
There is real-robot validation such as π0.5; D08 drops to 5 after the debate; world models are mostly demo-stage, and valuations run ahead of the evidence
OpenVLA-OFT already has closed-loop real-robot validation; D08 drops to 5, and most WAMs are still validated offline
D09 drops to 7, level with D06; D09 is still picked, as it is faster to start
What agents lack is continual learning; RLVR itself only resamples existing abilities
BLINK/VSI-Bench show that understanding still has many verifiable gaps
Pre-training is concentrated in a few institutions; evaluation is more open to academia
Continual learning is a capability agents clearly lack; scaffolding will be absorbed by models
The causal-verification problem in interpretability is, at root, still an evaluation problem
Fleet-type autonomous driving is closed to academia; embodied robotics is more open now

changes.argument_restated: Physical Atari: on non-contact tasks, swapping the robot body degraded all six games; the boundary is wider than contact/touch
changes.why: Unmodeled fine-grained physics differences are not limited to contact/touch; the weak zone of simulation is larger than I had drawn it; lowered by one notch

changes.argument_restated: AMI Labs/General Intuition valuations run ahead of decision-level evidence
changes.why: Independent corroboration across tables shows that my original low confidence was not just my own blind spot; both independent company cases show valuation coming before validation

held_despite.why: I accept the fact that s1 achieved a real gain with only 7 H100 GPU-hours, but D02 does not change: small compute improving efficiency is not the same as teaching new reasoning patterns; they are two separate things
I accept that reliable execution has decisive economic value under the tokens/W framework, but keep D02=5: economic importance is not an answer to where new capability comes from

still_disagree: X7: what remains with C3/C4 is a pure disagreement of values: whether reliable execution counts as a decisive lever or merely as an efficiency score. X6: what remains with C5/K3 is an empirical question: how much amplification really contributes to the long tail; wait for 2027-28 comparison data.
learned: K3's Physical Atari evidence widens the sim shortfall from contact/touch to any unmodeled fine-grained physics; it shows up even when a real robot is swapped for another unit built to the same drawings; the boundary is wider than I thought.
